plan_result.approach:
Test-only change. Background: in api/src/modules/export-templates/routes.ts, templateModule adds a preHandler hook. For every non-POST request (GET /, /active, /:id, /validations/:id) it calls requireTemplateAdmin(requireCurrentUser(request)). The preHandler runs after the root impersonation adoption, so an impersonated identity is checked, not the actor. TemplateService (template-service.ts) calls requireTemplateAdmin again. The existing tests in api/test/template-routes.test.ts mock only TemplateRepository.prototype and keep the real TemplateService. If the route hook is removed, the service check still returns 403, the repository mock is still not called, and every test passes. That is the gap this issue describes.

Design: add a new describe block in api/test/template-routes.test.ts, or a sibling file such as api/test/template-routes-guard.test.ts if the main file's shared app/mocks make isolation awkward. The block builds its own app through buildApp({ ..., templateService: stub }), the same way api/test/template-validation-errors.test.ts:120 injects a service. The stub is a plain object cast to TemplateService. Its read methods (history, active, get, validationStatus) are vi.fn()s that resolve to valid fixtures and do NO authorization, so the route hook is the only admin check left. Reuse the existing users, row and status fixtures and the harness helpers (sessionCookieFor, csrfHeaders, and the impersonation lookup seam) where possible. If buildTestApp cannot accept a templateService, either call buildApp directly with the same defaults or add an optional options parameter to the test harness. Do not change src.

What the tests assert: for each read route, (a) staff, support-only and disabled users get 403 FORBIDDEN and the stub method is never called; (b) an impersonating admin whose target is staff gets 403 and the stub is not called, which covers the reason the hook is preHandler rather than onRequest; (c) a positive control: a full admin gets 200 and the stub is called exactly once. The positive control proves the stub path is reachable, so the negative cases really exercise the route guard. Tag each with // @covers API-FR-EX-013 to match the file convention. requirements.index.json does not need a status change (EX-013 is already covered); at most, add the new test path to its tests list if that list names files.

Mutation evidence: the implementer temporarily deletes or no-ops the preHandler read guard in routes.ts, runs the new tests, and records the failing output (non-admin reads return 200 and the stub is called). They then restore the file and confirm green. The PR body shows the diff and the failing output. The guard mutation must not be committed. As a sanity check, the implementer also records that the pre-existing template-routes tests still pass under the same mutation. That shows the new test is the one closing the gap.

Classification SMALL: test-only, reversible, no production behaviour change. One implementer plus evidence-based acceptance. No architecture or cross-vendor review; the mutation run is the key evidence. Checks: the api vitest unit tier for the touched file(s), lint and typecheck (build) per AGENTS.md CI rules.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A new test builds the app with an injected TemplateService stub whose read methods (history, active, get, validationStatus) do no authorization. For each read route (GET /, /active, /:id, /validations/:id under /api/v1/admin/export-templates), staff, support-only and disabled sessions receive 403 with error.code FORBIDDEN, and the stub method is never called.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run the api vitest tier for the new or changed test file; all new cases pass on the unmodified routes.ts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An impersonating admin session whose target is a non-admin user receives 403 on the read routes with the service stub bypassed, and the stub is not called. This proves the read guard authorizes the adopted identity after impersonation.
acceptance_criteria.verification: The new test case passes; it uses the harness impersonation lookup seam that already exists in template-routes.test.ts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Positive control: with the same stub, a full admin receives 200 on each read route and the corresponding stub method is called. This shows the negative cases are rejected by the route guard, not by an unrelated failure.

Mutation shown: temporarily removing or no-opping the read preHandler guard in routes.ts makes the AC-1/AC-2 tests fail, while the pre-existing template-routes tests still pass under the same mutation. The mutation is reverted and not committed.
acceptance_criteria.verification: The PR description includes the mutation diff and the failing vitest output. The final diff leaves api/src/modules/export-templates/routes.ts unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No production source changes; repository CI gates stay green.
acceptance_criteria.verification: git diff limited to api/test/** (plus optional test-harness support and a requirements.index.json tests-path entry); lint, typecheck (build) and the api unit test tier pass.

contract.goal: Add tests to the export-template read routes that fail when the route-level admin guard (the preHandler requireTemplateAdmin for non-POST requests in api/src/modules/export-templates/routes.ts) is removed. The service-layer admin check must be bypassed in these tests, so the route guard is proven on its own.
non_goals: Changing route or service authorization behaviour, or removing the duplicated service-layer check.
Adding isolated-guard tests for the POST onRequest mutation guard; the existing tests that reject before body parsing already cover it.
Refactoring template-routes.test.ts or the test harness beyond what injecting the stub needs.
Covering other admin modules' route guards.

risks: The stub service may not fully satisfy TemplateService's type or what app.ts needs at boot. registerTemplateValidationWorker(app, templateService) runs at startup, so the stub may need no-op worker-related methods. Mitigation: a typed partial stub with the methods the worker registration touches, or start from a real TemplateService and override only the read methods with vi.spyOn on that instance.

Fixtures that do not match the response schemas could make the admin positive control fail through serialization rather than auth. Reuse the existing row/status fixtures, which the current tests already use with 200 responses.

Shared vi.spyOn state in template-routes.test.ts: spying on TemplateRepository.prototype at describe scope could leak across describe blocks. A separate app instance with an injected stub avoids prototype spies. If this stays in the same file, keep the new mocks instance-scoped.
If the POST onRequest hook and the read preHandler hook were later merged, a mutation run that removes only one of them could be misread. The mutation must target the read preHandler specifically.
